The New Project

The L.S.D. World

With The LSD Project, DatsJustice takes a cinematic leap into the emotional extremes of luxury, desire, temptation, ambition, addiction, power, and escape. Released through RSRL Music Group and RockLan One Music Group, the project brings Hip-Hop, rock, punk, rage, and pop influences into one rebellious and cohesive body of work. The title, Luxury, Sex, and Drugs, may initially sound like a celebration of excess. Beneath the surface, the project examines what happens when indulgence becomes identity and desire begins controlling the person who believed they were in control.

“LSD is not about the surface. It is about what luxury does to your spirit when you start chasing status, what sex does to your ego when desire becomes power, and what drugs do to your mind when escape becomes identity. It is about the cost of everything we think we want.”

DatsJustice, RockLan One Magazine

That emotional duality exists throughout the project. Pleasure and pain occupy the same room. Confidence hides insecurity, attraction becomes manipulation, escape becomes dependence, and success carries consequences that are rarely visible from the outside. Rather than presenting himself as a flawless character, DatsJustice places his contradictions at the center of the music, and the result feels less like a traditional album and more like a psychological journey. The LSD Project is coming soon. No release date has been announced.

Toxic Energy

“Toxic,” the project’s lead single, arrives as an explosive declaration of individuality. Driven by distorted 808s, aggressive percussion, heavy guitar textures, and industrial energy, the track channels rage, self-awareness, and unapologetic confidence into one relentless performance. It is both a warning and a celebration, reminding listeners that self-acceptance does not always arrive quietly.

Listen: Toxic

Faded Connections

“Faded All Day” slows the project down and turns inward. The record examines a relationship gradually losing its clarity beneath constant smoking, emotional avoidance, and miscommunication. It is one of the project’s most vulnerable moments, a record that feels painfully familiar to anyone who has watched a relationship fade without knowing exactly when the separation began.

Listen: Faded All Day

The Story

About DatsJustice

From the streets of Flushing, Queens, through Virginia, and into the creative fire of Atlanta, DatsJustice has transformed every chapter of his life into another layer of his artistry. Each relocation represented more than a change of scenery. It became an evolution in sound, perspective, identity, and ambition.

Queens gave him grit, grounding his creativity in the raw energy of East Coast lyricism and relentless hustle. Virginia introduced a more reflective side, allowing introspection, melody, and emotional storytelling to become central parts of his creative language. Atlanta became the final ignition point, placing him inside one of the most influential music communities in the world and giving him the freedom to experiment without limitation.

“Each place changed me. The sound, the people, and the energy all became part of my story.”

That story now lives inside every record he creates, carrying pieces of the environments, experiences, and emotional battles that shaped him. DatsJustice does not approach music as a performer searching for a temporary moment. He approaches it as an innovator building an entire world. His records move between aggression, melody, vulnerability, indulgence, confidence, and chaos, reflecting the unpredictable journey that made him the artist he is today.

In Atlanta, inside studios, underground venues, creative collectives, and late night recording sessions, he surrounded himself with artists, engineers, and producers who viewed music as something limitless. Instead of copying the sounds around him, he absorbed the energy and transformed it into something personal. His music now reflects Atlanta’s heartbeat. It is rhythmic, unpredictable, rebellious, emotionally charged, and unapologetically alive. Beneath the raw energy is a calculated artistic vision, balancing chaos with clarity and instinct with intention.

What separates DatsJustice from many of his peers is not simply his ability to move between genres. It is the authenticity behind each transition. His sound changes because his emotions change, not because he is chasing whatever happens to be popular. In an industry increasingly guided by algorithms, recycled aesthetics, and momentary trends, DatsJustice is committed to creating from a place of truth. His music does not ask permission to be understood. It invites listeners to enter the experience and decide what it means for themselves.

RockLan One Magazine · Volume 3, Issue 6 · Cover Story

Luxury. Sex. Drugs. And The Art of Fearless Reinvention

From Flushing, Queens to Virginia to Atlanta, DatsJustice has turned every chapter of his life into fuel for a fearless, genre bending artistic evolution. The full feature follows The LSD Project, the lead single “Toxic,” and the brand being built around the music. Photography by Azu Studios.

“Atlanta gave me space to experiment. You can be weird here. You can be real. You can build something from nothing, and the city will feel you when it is honest.”
“I create from feeling. The beat tells me what to say, and I never force it. When I am not feeling it, it will not sound right.”
Billboard Magazine: The Interview +

Billboard Magazine: In-Depth Interview with DatsJustice

Billboard: You’ve been called a multifaceted innovator, artist, and trendsetter. How do you personally describe who DatsJustice is?

DatsJustice: I’m a creator, plain and simple. Whether it’s music, visuals, or fashion, my goal is to connect with people by being authentic and fearless. I like to challenge norms and inspire others to embrace their uniqueness. My story, my struggles, and my vision, that’s what makes me who I am.

Billboard: Let’s talk about your roots. How did growing up in Queens, Atlanta, and Virginia influence your style and sound?

DatsJustice: Each place shaped me in a different way. Queens taught me the grind, Atlanta gave me the culture and a broader perspective, and Virginia gave me time to experiment and reflect. Those experiences blend into everything I create. It’s like having a diverse toolkit that helps me approach music and life with versatility.

Billboard: Your music breaks genre barriers. How would you explain your sound to someone who’s never heard it?

DatsJustice: My sound is fluid. I blend rap, rock, punk, and pop. It’s high-energy and emotional, with no boundaries. I want people to feel something when they listen, whether it’s hype, introspective, or just having fun. Songs like “Faded All Day” and “Toxic” show that balance between vulnerability and confidence. Both are key tracks from my upcoming project L.S.D. (Luxury, Sex, and Drugs).

Billboard: “Faded All Day” and “Toxic” have become fan favorites. What’s the story behind these tracks?

DatsJustice: “Faded All Day” comes from a personal place. It’s about relationships and how our habits affect them. It’s reflective but relatable. On the other hand, “Toxic” is unapologetic. It’s about owning your flaws and turning them into strengths. Both songs show different sides of me and my journey.

Billboard: You’re known for your high-energy live shows. What’s your mindset when you step on stage?

DatsJustice: It’s all about connection. I feed off the crowd’s energy, and I want them to leave feeling like they were part of something unique. My performances aren’t just about music; they’re about creating an unforgettable experience. I want people to vibe with me and feel inspired when they leave.

Billboard: Your single “I’m Him” feels like an anthem for self-confidence. What inspired it?

DatsJustice: “I’m Him” is about claiming your space and owning who you are. It’s a reminder to myself and anyone listening that we all have something special to offer. It’s not about arrogance; it’s about believing in your worth even when the world doubts you. It’s an empowering track.

Billboard: Fashion is another big part of your identity. How does your clothing line tie into your artistry?

DatsJustice: Fashion is another way for me to tell stories. My clothing line reflects individuality and creativity, just like my music. It’s not just about looking good, it’s about wearing something that represents who you are. I’m focused on creating pieces that feel bold and authentic, like everything else I do.

Billboard: What can you tell us about L.S.D. (Luxury, Sex, and Drugs)? What inspired this project?

DatsJustice: It is going to be something completely different. It dives deep into themes of indulgence, desire, and escapism, inspired by the highs and lows of life. Each track is like a chapter in a story, exploring these themes in ways that are raw and relatable. I wanted to challenge traditional storytelling in music and invite fans to reflect on their own experiences. This project is bold, and I think it will resonate deeply with listeners.

Billboard: What do you think makes you stand out in today’s music scene?

DatsJustice: My versatility and authenticity. I’m not afraid to experiment or be vulnerable in my music. I bring a unique perspective, and I’m intentional about every detail, from lyrics to visuals. People can feel when something is real, and that’s what sets me apart.

Billboard: What advice would you give to independent artists trying to break into the industry?

DatsJustice: Stay true to yourself, first and foremost. Don’t get caught up trying to imitate what’s already out there. Learn the business side, branding, marketing, and building a strong team are essential. And don’t be afraid to take risks or fail. Every setback is just a setup for growth.

Billboard: What’s next for you beyond L.S.D.?

DatsJustice: I’ve got a lot cooking, new music, visuals, and collaborations that I’m really hyped about. The clothing line is growing too. I’m focused on leveling up and bringing something fresh to my audience. It is all about elevating everything I do.

Billboard: Lastly, what’s your ultimate vision as an artist?

DatsJustice: My goal is to leave a legacy that inspires people to be fearless and embrace their creativity. I want to create art that stands the test of time and connects with people on a deeper level. It’s about impact, not just success. I want to make sure that everything I do has meaning.

Billboard: Thank you for sharing your journey with us, DatsJustice. We’re excited to see what’s ahead.

DatsJustice: Thank you. It’s been real. I appreciate the love.

Complex Magazine: The Versatile Innovator +

DatsJustice: The Versatile Innovator Reshaping Hip-Hop

Complex Magazine

Growing up with roots in Flushing Queens, New York, and Atlanta, Georgia, DatsJustice embodies a blend of grit and creativity that defines his artistry. The contrasts of his upbringing, coupled with a stint in Virginia, laid the foundation for a sound that’s as diverse as his journey. “Music wasn’t just something I listened to; it was a way to process life,” he says. From these experiences, DatsJustice emerged as a multifaceted artist unafraid to explore and innovate. His ability to seamlessly adapt to different environments and incorporate various influences sets him apart in a crowded music landscape.

Blurring Boundaries with Sound

When asked how he developed his signature style, a seamless fusion of rap, rock, punk, and pop, DatsJustice credits his eclectic musical diet. “I grew up listening to everything from Jay-Z to Green Day to Prince,” he explains. “That mix helped me see music as a limitless canvas.” His refusal to stick to a single genre is a deliberate choice, allowing him to craft songs that resonate with a broad audience. Whether he’s channeling raw rap energy or tapping into punk vibes, he lets the beat guide him, resulting in a sound that defies categorization.

Tracks like “Faded All Day” and “Toxic” showcase his ability to balance vulnerability and boldness. The former delves into the struggles of relationships strained by personal habits, offering a narrative that’s both introspective and relatable. “Faded All Day” captures the push and pull of trying to maintain connections while battling personal demons. Meanwhile, “Toxic” embraces imperfections unapologetically, diving deep into themes of self-awareness, emotional struggles, and the beauty in flaws. “It’s about owning who you are, flaws and all,” he explains. With a haunting melody and raw, introspective lyrics, “Toxic” captures the duality of vulnerability and strength. “I wanted to create something that felt real, something people could see themselves in, whether they’re facing inner battles or just trying to accept themselves,” DatsJustice shares.

Declaring Identity Through Music

DatsJustice’s music is deeply personal, often serving as a mirror of his own experiences and a declaration of his identity. “Music is my therapy,” he says. Tracks like “Toxic” act as both self-reflection and an invitation for listeners to own their own identities. “I want people to feel empowered when they hear it, like they can conquer anything,” he adds. His music is more than entertainment; it’s a journey that invites listeners to find strength in their vulnerabilities and pride in their uniqueness.

Beyond the Music: Building a Legacy

For DatsJustice, artistry doesn’t end with music. His clothing line serves as an extension of his creative vision. “Fashion is another way I express myself,” he says. “It’s bold, edgy, and authentic, just like my music.” By blending streetwear with designer influences, he’s crafting a brand that makes a statement. His designs reflect his music’s themes, resonating with fans who value individuality and self-expression.

His dedication to the independent artist movement reflects his understanding of the industry’s shifting landscape. “It’s a great time to be an independent artist,” he notes. “Platforms like social media and streaming let you connect directly with your audience. It’s all about staying true to yourself while navigating the business side smartly.” His focus on maintaining creative control and building genuine connections with fans underscores his commitment to authenticity.

Energizing the Stage

DatsJustice’s live performances are as dynamic as his music. “Energy is everything,” he says. “When I’m on stage, I’m not just performing; I’m sharing an experience with the crowd.” His shows are characterized by high energy, crowd engagement, and memorable moments. From encouraging crowd participation to delivering electrifying performances, he leaves audiences saying, “That was something different.” His ability to connect with the crowd stems from his genuine love for performing and his desire to create unforgettable experiences.

Looking Ahead

With his upcoming project, L.S.D. (Luxury, Sex, and Drugs), DatsJustice promises to push boundaries even further. “Expect tracks that tap into different sides of who I am,” he teases. The project will explore themes of indulgence, self-discovery, and the complexities of modern life. Beyond music, he’s focused on collaborations and expanding his brand.

Advice for Aspiring Artists

DatsJustice’s advice for aspiring artists is simple yet profound: “Stay true to yourself,” he says. “Learn the business, build a solid team, and always be willing to adapt. Most importantly, believe in your vision. If you don’t, nobody else will.” His journey is a testament to the power of authenticity, resilience, and a relentless commitment to one’s craft.

DatsJustice isn’t just crafting songs, he’s creating a movement. With his versatility, bold vision, and unrelenting drive, he’s redefining what it means to be an artist in today’s music landscape. As he continues to inspire and innovate, the world is watching as he reshapes the culture, one boundary-breaking track at a time.

The Brand

Store

Coming Soon · The LSD Collection

Beyond the music, DatsJustice is building a brand designed to match the scale of his artistic vision. The upcoming merchandise collection connected to the deluxe edition of The LSD Project will extend the project into fashion, lifestyle, visual storytelling, and collectible culture. The collection is expected to include bold streetwear, statement pieces, and limited edition designs inspired by the project’s lyrics, imagery, attitude, and emotional themes.

Instead of treating merchandise as a basic promotional product, DatsJustice views it as another form of artistic expression. The clothing will allow supporters to carry pieces of the album’s universe into their everyday lives. Each design becomes another chapter in the story, transforming the music into something listeners can wear, collect, and identify with.

“Listeners want authenticity, and independent creators are giving them that. You do not need a machine to make meaningful art. You need vision.”
